blind/rnn: A recurrent network reads a sentence one token per step, so the order comes built in: dog is first because it is read first.
blind/all: Self-attention dropped the steps. Every token scores every token at once, and nothing in a score says where a token sits.
blind/one: Take dog bites man, and one number from each token's output.
blind/swap: Now swap the first and last words: man bites dog. Every token brings the same query, key and value as before.
blind/same: So bites gets exactly the same output, and dog and man keep theirs too: the outputs just trade places with their tokens.
blind/bag: To attention, a sentence is a bag of tokens, like words shaken in a bag: all there, in no order. Two sentences with opposite meanings look the same.
add/fix: The fix came in the same paper that dropped the steps. In 2017, Ashish Vaswani and colleagues gave every position a vector of its own, and added it to the embedding of the token there.
add/table: Stack those vectors as the rows of a second table, P: row zero for the first position, row one for the second, and so on.
add/dog: Dog's embedding is the point one, two. Draw it as an arrow from the origin.
add/sum0: At position zero, add row zero of P, which is zero, one, tip to tail: dog lands at one, three.
add/sum2: At position two, add row two instead, one, minus one: now dog lands at two, one.
add/rows: Two lookups, then: E by which token it is, and P by where it sits.
add/differ: The same word now enters at a different point in each place, so its query, key and value change with it, and attention can tell dog bites man from man bites dog.
learned/learned: The numbers in P are learned, the same way the embeddings are, so vectors like these are also called position embeddings.
learned/tmax: P needs a row for every position the model will see. Write T max for the most tokens it reads at once: T for tokens, as in attention, and max for the most. So P is T max by d.
learned/size: Say a model reads up to one thousand and twenty four tokens, each of seven hundred sixty eight numbers. Then P holds one thousand and twenty four times seven hundred sixty eight: seven hundred eighty six thousand, four hundred thirty two learned numbers.
learned/end: And a token past the last row gets no position vector at all. So T max is the longest input the model can read.
